title: Booking Earl King and Joe Turner
summary: He booked Earl King and Joe Turner for years; Turner lived in New Orleans after his Chicago divorce and later toured overseas.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You booked, you booked Earl King, didn't you?
Yeah, I booked Earl King from any time. Okay, you told me. When you had my mother-in-law out, two or three more numbers, I got up. Yeah. The mother-in-law are very good friends.
You told me, you had a couple of years to do dough up in Brooklyn, and you also booked Joe Turner, I see you.
Right, I booked Joe Turner for years. Joe and I were very close friends, I booked it for years.
And so did you work around here? Oh yeah, he lived here.
He bought a house at town, he made a woman from here. But now, he's met another woman in California since then, but he made a girl from here. So how did you live here? When did you live here?
You know, from when? Oh, no, no. Mid-50s? I mean. No, it wasn't 50.

No, it had to be in his 60s, I believe. It had to be, it could have been 59 into the 60s, I'm just guessing now. But he got a divorce from his wife in Chicago around, probably around 56 or 57, I believe. And then he, they buy the property up, he got the money, he met this woman here. They stayed together for maybe 3 or 4 or 5, I don't know. So then he went to California, in fact he called me once in a while, he's met again in California. You get a lot of wicked to them overseas, they put the old package together, you know, Muddy Water, Joe Turner and somebody else, you know, and you go across the seas and just mop up. They always do.
